# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_014_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 14

**1** Jesus said to them: "If you fast [нностеуе], you will bring sin [нове] upon yourselves.

**2** If you pray [шлнл], you will be condemned [тсаве].

**3** If you give alms [рпроснпора], you will harm [рпетноч] your spirits [пна].

**4** When you go into any land and walk about in the countryside, if they receive [шелеет] you, eat [оуом] what they set before you. Heal [талчо] the sick among them.

**5** For what goes into your mouth will not defile [ркосос] you. Rather, what comes out of your mouth will defile you."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- The opening triad (fasting, prayer, almsgiving) directly answers Saying 6's question: these practices are rejected absolutely
- *нове*: sin, transgression
- *тсаве*: to condemn; prayer done wrongly brings condemnation
- *рпетноч*: to harm/damage; the verb is strong
- *пна*: spirit, breath — inner being harmed by improper almsgiving
- *шелеет*: to receive, welcome; hospitality context
- *талчо*: to heal; the positive mission — healing replaces the rejected rituals
- V.5 closely parallels Matt 15:11; Mark 7:15 — the purity saying
- The contrast: not what enters (dietary law) but what exits (speech/intention) defiles
